WORK EFFORT PLANNING NOTE
Proposal Team | Submission Readiness Guide
Prepared for internal use • Revision 2.4
This note helps proposal coordinators prepare a concise record of staffing effort before the final submission package is assembled. It is a planning aid, not a budget narrative or approval form.
WHY REVIEWERS NEED IT
Reviewers should be able to see the planned work commitment without searching through technical sections. The record should identify who is involved and how effort is distributed across the proposed period.
WHAT TO CHECK
Count every contributor, including unpaid collaborators and positions that have not yet been filled. Use one row per person or role, and keep names consistent with the budget and management plan.
Keep effort values separate from salary, travel, equipment, and indirect-cost figures. Those details belong in their own schedules and should not be copied into this working note.
RECORDING CONVENTION
Enter effort by proposal years rather than fiscal years. Use fractions of a person-work-year, apply the same rounding convention throughout, and mark an unpaid commitment only when the proposal rules permit it.
Do not add technical narrative to an effort grid. Roles, responsibilities, milestones, and scientific rationale remain in the main proposal sections.
HANDOFF
Before submission, one coordinator verifies the names and totals while a second checks the source files. Record unresolved questions in the team log rather than guessing at a value.
REFERENCE
Current templates are posted at https://proposals.northstar-lab.example/work-effort. Send access questions to proposaldesk@northstar-lab.example.
 FINAL REMINDER
The blank grid is for later allocation notes only. Leave every cell empty when inserting it.
